assets.content:
KANTYNA NOVA — APPROVED COPY (course titles are set, do not rewrite)

Tagline: One seating. One menu. One evening.
About: A single table set once a night. One tasting, one wine flight, cooked and served by the two of us. The room is dark and quiet by design, so the plate is the only thing lit.
Voice: first person plural, plain, understated. Never salesy.

THE TASTING — fourteen courses, in order (page one of the menu)
1. Oyster, brown butter, sea lettuce — Cold, from the first minute of the evening.
2. Smoked mussel, celeriac, dulse — Smoke, then the sea underneath it.
3. Cured fluke, buttermilk, green apple — Cured that morning, dressed at the pass.
4. Sea urchin, potato custard, brioche — Set warm, a shard of brioche to break it.
5. Roasted beetroot, aged goat, walnut — Roasted whole in the ash, cut to order.
6. Hand-cut tagliatelle, brown crab, chilli — Rolled that afternoon, crab picked by hand.
7. Seared scallop, cauliflower, brown butter — One scallop, seared hard, brown butter to finish.
8. Halibut, leek, mussel cream — Poached soft, the cream built from the shells.
9. Duck, salsify, blackberry — Aged on the bone, blackberry from the reduction.
10. Dry-aged beef, bone marrow, burnt onion — Forty days, marrow and onion beside it.
11. Aged comté, honeycomb — Kept until it is ready, honey from up the coast.
12. Brown butter tart, sea salt — The pastry we make every day.
13. Chocolate, olive oil, malt — Dark, oil poured at the table, malt for the crunch.
14. Petit fours — Whatever we baked that morning. [NOTE: this course has never been photographed]

HOURS (for the reservations page)
Wednesday to Sunday. One seating a night. Doors at 6:30, seated at 7:00. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
The private dining side seats a smaller room on request.

RESERVATION WORDING (approved)
"One seating a night, and the room is small. Book the evening and let it happen — we will hold the table from 6:30. If your plans change, tell us as early as you can; there is no third of us to fill an empty seat."

THE DECK — how the price is built up (final slide, plain, price never a feature)
"The tasting is one hundred and eighty five dollars a guest. The wine pairing is another ninety five. That is the evening: fourteen courses, one flight, cooked and served by the two of us. There is no cover, no service charge added at the table, and nothing else to buy. Eighteen covers a night is the whole business, so the price is what it takes to set this table once and set it well."

assets.defect_engineered: the printed card reads as four tidy blocks (guest name, course, wine designation, allergen line) plus a picture well, but the file is set with name/course/allergen as ONE continuous text story (far coarser frame granularity than the printed page implies), and the WINE DESIGNATION sits in its own FIXED-WIDTH frame sized to the printer's own short sample text ('Muscadet 2021') so a longer designation stops rendering mid-word at the frame edge with no visible spill; the media box equals the trim so there is ZERO bleed and a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the private-dining printer's existing pairing-card press PDF (flat, single sample record; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template).

Document: single card, 127 x 89 mm LANDSCAPE, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. This is the file the room's printer already prints one card per guest from.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (four apparent text blocks + a picture):
- Left half: a rectangular PICTURE WELL holding the dish photograph, full-bleed to the left trim edge in appearance.
- Top-right: the GUEST NAME in a transitional display serif, large (sample text: 'Marta').
- Under it: a COURSE line in a humanist text face (sample text: 'Seared scallop, cauliflower, brown butter').
- Under that: the WINE DESIGNATION in the same text face, italic (sample text: 'Muscadet 2021').
- Bottom-right strip: an ALLERGEN line, small caps, quiet (sample text: 'Shellfish').

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The GUEST NAME, the COURSE line and the ALLERGEN line are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame flowing top to bottom down the right column — they are NOT three separately addressable frames, so the frame granularity a conversion exposes is far coarser than the four tidy blocks the printed card implies.
- The WINE DESIGNATION is the exception: it sits in its OWN separate text frame, but that frame is a FIXED width sized exactly around the printer's short sample string 'Muscadet 2021'. It does not grow, it does not push the following line down, and it does not spill anywhere visible: a longer designation (a producer + an appellation + a vintage) simply stops rendering at the right frame edge, mid-word, on that record alone.
- The PICTURE WELL is a real rectangular graphic frame (a picture CAN be bound into it — one per guest — unlike a decorative device), at roughly the ratio 63.5 x 89 mm (the left half of the card).

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called; the shortfall must be reported, not quietly dropped.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): GUEST_NAME | COURSE | WINE_DESIGNATION | ALLERGENS | DISH_PICTURE

Colours: Cellar Black #14110F ground and picture surround, Warm Bone #E9E2D4 guest name and course, Aged Brass #A6875A the hairline under the name and the wine designation italic, Ash Stone #7C7468 the allergen line.
